desc:
A row of seats is given by seats: seats[i] = 1 means seat i is taken and 0 means it is free. At least one seat is taken and at least one is free.

You will choose a free seat. The distance from your seat i to the closest taken seat is the minimum of |i - j| over all taken seats j. Return the largest such distance you can achieve.

seats = [1,0,0,0,1,0,1]  -> 2
seats = [1,0,0,0]        -> 3
seats = [0,1]            -> 1

In the first example sit at seat 2: the taken seats 0 and 4 are both 2 away.
constraints: At least one 0 and at least one 1 appear
hints: Only the free stretches (gaps) between taken seats matter. What are the different kinds of gaps?
A gap between two taken seats is best used in its middle. A gap at the very start or very end of the row has a taken seat on only one side.

For a gap bounded on both sides by taken seats at positions a < b, the best distance is (b - a) // 2. For a gap at the left end the best seat is seat 0, with distance equal to the index of the first taken seat; symmetrically for the right end.
editorial: Scan the row and remember the position of the last taken seat. Three kinds of gaps exist. Before the first taken seat at index f, the best choice is seat 0 and the distance is f. After the last taken seat at index l, the best choice is the final seat with distance n - 1 - l. Between two consecutive taken seats a < b, the best choice is the middle, with distance (b - a) // 2.
The answer is the maximum over all gaps. The reason end gaps are handled differently is that they lack the second neighbour that halves the distance. One pass and O(1) extra memory.
